prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset: one original childhood portrait of Jackie Leven for a dark biographical homage website, a coherent fourth image in the supplied three-portrait series.

Input roles:
Image 1 is the ONLY subject/identity/age reference: a childhood photograph reproduced on a cropped sepia book cover. Use the actual child's face, eyes, eyebrows, nose, mouth, short straight hair and fringe visible in this source. Completely discard all lettering, strips, collage, book graphics, sepia coloration and photographic background.
Images 2, 3 and 4 are ONLY references for the existing portrait series' drawing language, limited neutral grey palette, compressed dark values and disappearing edges. DO NOT use their adult facial anatomy, age, hairstyles, facial hair, clothing details or props. Do not create a de-aged version of these adults.

Subject: the same child as in photo 1, at the same apparent childhood age. Preserve his individual proportions: large alert eyes, distinct slightly asymmetric eyebrows, straight prominent nose, rounded youthful cheeks and natural mouth; straight dark short hair with an uneven blunt fringe. Keep his serious, curious, quietly watchful expression. Natural youthful features, not a miniature adult, not an infant, not an idealized cute child. No facial hair or adult lines.
Composition: a NEW head-and-shoulders portrait in a vertical 4:5 format. Pull back from the source's extremely tight cropped face so that the full crown, both sides of the hair, neck and a suggestion of shoulders are visible. Retain a gentle three-quarter head angle and the source's alert gaze. Modestly turn the shoulders independently of the head for a natural pose. Clothing only suggested by sparse marks of a simple dark crew-neck top; no emblem, pattern, uniform detail, hands or objects. Leave dark breathing room around the entire head. Lower shoulders and chest become sparse gestural traces then disappear into the background.

Style: match the three approved series portraits, especially image 3's economical dry-brush face and image 2's broad broken hair/clothing strokes. A drawn/painted ink illustration with expressive physical dry-brush gestures and a few large matte grey pigment shapes, retaining recognizable anatomy. Use irregular torn brush edges, restrained directional hatching and unworked dark spaces. Simplify shadows and highlights; don't render photographic skin, individual hairs or fabric detail. The face should read through a few well-placed strokes and calm light/shadow shapes. No excessive smooth photographic modelling, no glossy digital painting, no mechanical vector-poster shapes, no engraving filigree, no embossed pebbly texture applied uniformly. Allow the softer actual anatomy of a child's face without making the drawing sentimental.

Palette and light: dark anthracite #0d0f12 background seamlessly matching the website, strictly neutral charcoal and muted grey highlights. NO brown, sepia, beige, cream, yellow or vintage-paper cast. Broad highlights roughly #62676b to #777b7e, very few accents up to #85888b; shadows merge with the near-black ground. No white. Match the subdued, watermark-like presence of images 2-4. Keep natural positive light/shadow: pupils, nostrils and mouth are dark within the facial light planes, not a photographic negative. Quiet and alive, not ghostly, spectral or gothic.
All outer edges should dissolve organically into almost flat #0d0f12 with no frame, halo or paper border. Most of the canvas stays dark; the face is still legible at webpage size.
One image, not a contact sheet. No text, names, lettering, logos, signature, book layout, labels, instruments, buildings or other people.
status: user-favorite; preserve while exploring an en-face variant
